numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When using `HDFStore.select` with a `where` query that applies `<` or `<=` to a `datetime64`/`timedelta64` column, the selection incorrectly includes the `NaT` rows because `NaT` is stored as `iNaT` (int64 minimum), which compares as less than every real value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: `HDFStore.select` should exclude `NaT` rows for `<`/`<=` comparisons, matching the equivalent in-memory comparison (i.e., guard the predicate as `((col != iNaT) & (col <op> val))`).
trigger_conditions: Using `HDFStore.select` with a `where` string containing a `<` or `<=` filter on a column whose kind starts with `datetime` or `timedelta` (datetime64/timedelta64).
The filtered column contains missing values (`NaT`), stored internally as `iNaT` (int64 min).

input_output_examples.input: df = DataFrame({"col": to_datetime(["2020-01-01 00:00:00", "2020-01-01 00:00:02", NaT]).as_unit("s"), "pos": range(3)})\nstore.append("t", df, data_columns=True, index=False)\nstore.select("t", where="col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01'")["pos"].tolist()
input_output_examples.source: PR#68031 reproducer in PR body / kept whole

oracle_clues: Passage states the in-memory comparison never matches the missing (`NaT`) rows for the equivalent `<` query.
Fix described: `BinOp.generate` emits `((col != iNaT) & (col <op> val))` for `<`/`<=` when the column kind starts with `datetime`/`timedelta`, while `>`/`>=` need no such guard.

category_specific_evidence: PR#68031 reproducer: df has a datetime column created as to_datetime(["2020-01-01 00:00:00", "2020-01-01 00:00:02", NaT]).as_unit("s"); after storing and selecting with where="col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01'", the result returned positions [0, 2] but the expected was [0].
Bug mechanism described: datetime-like columns are stored as int64 with NaT as iNaT (int64 minimum), so an unguarded "less than" predicate matches the NaT rows.

Correct handling described for code generation: BinOp.generate now emits ((col != iNaT) & (col < val)) for self.op in ("<","<=") when the column kind is datetime64/timedelta64; for ">"/">=" no such guard is needed.

Code change location: pandas/core/computation/pytables.py generate(): if self.op in ("<","<=") and kind.startswith(("datetime","timedelta")), it returns f"(({lhs} != {iNaT}) & ({lhs} {self.op} {val}))"; otherwise it returns f"({lhs} {self.op} {val})".

Test: test_select_ordering_comparison_skips_nat_on_index parametrizes op in ["<","<="] and constructs a DatetimeIndex(["2020-01-01","2020-01-03", pd.NaT]); it expects that where="index {op} '2020-01-02'" yields expected=df.iloc[:1] (NaT row skipped for "<"; test asserts frame equality).

New test parametrization covers NaT in multiple datetime/timedelta representations: pd.to_datetime([... , pd.NaT]) (rhs "2020-01-02"), the same with .as_unit("s") (rhs "2020-01-02"), timezone-aware datetimes via .tz_localize("UTC") (rhs "2020-01-02 00:00:00+00:00"), and timedeltas via pd.to_timedelta(["1s","3s", pd.NaT]) with rhs "2s".
Correct predicate handling is explicitly stated in commit message: ">"/">=" need no guard because the incorrect matching issue is tied to "less than" ordering with iNaT being int64 minimum.
reproduction_risks: Only the "<"/"<=" path is described as requiring the NaT guard; ">"/">=" are stated as needing no guard, so a reproduction that tests only "<"/"<=" is necessary to observe the failure described.
The NaT issue is specifically for columns whose kind starts with "datetime" or "timedelta" (datetime64/timedelta64); reproductions on other dtypes may not trigger the described behavior.
The mechanism depends on NaT being stored as iNaT (int64 minimum), so reproductions must include missing values (NaT) in the filtered column.
